newsitem.title: BELGIUM: ALCATEL BELL TO MOVE A BELGIAN FACTORY TO FRANCE.
newsitem.headline: ALCATEL BELL TO MOVE A BELGIAN FACTORY TO FRANCE.

text.p: Alcatel Bell, the Belgian subsidiary of France's Alcatel Alsthom , said on Thursday it was ending Alcatel activity at its Colfontaine plant, transferring almost all of it to a factory in France.

"It was announced at a works council that at the end of September the factory of Alcatel Bell in Colfontaine (near Mons) will cease its Alcatel activities," Alcatel Bell spokesman Piet Van Speybroeck told Reuters.
He said that in the meantime the company would look for a candidate from outside the Alcatel group to take over the plant, which employs 189 people.
The Colfontaine plant mostly makes switches, used in office telephone systems, and has a minor activity in the area of pay phones.

Van Speybroeck said that the "labour content" of the switch business had fallen dramatically and in the last three to four years the number of people needed to do the job had fallen by up to 50 percent. The Colfontaine plant already shed more than 100 jobs at the end of 1995.
Because of "economies of scale" therefore, switch making at Colfontaine would be transferred to a factory in France.
Colfontaine's minor pay phone activities would be moved to Turkey, Van Speybroeck added,.
Belgium is still seething over a sudden decision by French car maker Renault to close its profitable factory in Vilvoorde with the loss of 3,100 jobs.
The changes were part of a global restructuring plan announced by Alcatel Alsthom in September 1995.
In a statement Alcatel also announced other measures aimed at reinforcing Alcatel Bell's technological, commercial and industrial position.
These included cost cutting and improving effectiveness by outsourcing some administrative and support jobs, and cutting 325 jobs - 250 of which would be workers over the age of 50.

However investments in 1997 would amount to 7.2 billion Belgian francs, little changed from 1995 and 1996, and the company would continue to take on specialists, expecting to recruit 250 more in 1997.
Alcatel Bell had a non-conolidated operating loss of more than 500 million Belgian francs in 1996, mainly as a result of falling sales on certain export markets, the statement said.

It said that under the new organisation of the Alcatel Group, the Belgian company must concentrate on activities where it could offer maximum added value, for example engineering, marketing and support for all the divisions, and coordinating the interests of Alcatel in 26 countries.
